# 2 Baruch Chapter 37 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 2 Baruch Chapter 37 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 37:1 — "you are able to interpret / please interpret"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "you-are-able to-interpret for-me" | Literal: Syriac affirms God's capacity |
| LOGOS | "you are able to interpret for me" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "please interpret this vision for me" | Omits the "you are able" and makes a direct request |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "you are able to interpret for me" (EMET/LOGOS). The Syriac phrase is an expression of confidence in God's interpretive power, not merely a polite request. PNEUMA's simplification loses this theological note.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS. Theological nuance preserved.

---
